NYC's CTC has had a positive effect on smoking prevalence and quit ratios among adults with serious mental illness (SMI) and those without SMI.5 Trends in smoking prevalence and quitting among those with SMI are important to understand because of the excess burden of smoking-related illness among those with mental illnesses.6–8 The NYC CTC has included a focus on mental illness since its inception, and the city is the largest in the USA to offer free cessation medications to all smokers,

NYC CTC is associated with a 2.6 percentage point reduction (95% CI −4.1 to −1.2) in adult smoking prevalence and a 1.8 percentage point reduction in serious psychological distress (SPD) prevalence (95% CI 1.1 to −2.4) over 10 years.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prevalence of smoking among those with mental health conditions is not declining as fast as the general population in New York.
smoking prevalence among adults with serious mental illness in NYC has fallen substantially since 2003, but remains higher than in those without such illness.
NYC has seen significant progress in reducing smoking among those with serious psychological distress.
